newsitem.title: USA: Cabot concerned about Europe carbon market.
newsitem.headline: Cabot concerned about Europe carbon market.

text.p: Cabot Corp on Tuesday said it expected improving volumes for its tantalum business in the coming months but it was concerned about the European market for carbon black.
The specialty chemical and materials supplier said its tantalum business showed increased shipments in March and customers order rates were improving.
"We believe the tantalum business will see improving volumes in the coming months. Our fumed silica and (liquefied natural gas) markets appear healthy," the company said in a statement.

"However, we are concerned with our European carbon black market, where we are exposed to the effects of a strengthening dollar and of our inability to pass higher costs on to our customers," it said.
The company said its Microelectronics Materials Division is operating profitably and should turn a small profit in 1997 even though a slowdown in the semiconductor industry has held back growth.
On Tuesday, Cabot said its first-quarter profit fell to $0.38 a share on a diluted basis from earnings of $0.51 in the same period a year earlier. Sales fell to $432 million from $491 million.
Cabot shares dipped 1/8 to 24-1/4 on Tuesday.
